ai_summary: Scotland continues to demonstrate deep structural decoupling from the wider grid, pairing world-class renewable potential with persistent transmission bottlenecks. Across the system, total GB wind output currently stands at 13.1 GW, driven substantially by an estimated Scottish wind output of 4.7 GW, which accounts for 46.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This surge in clean generation drives Scottish carbon intensity to a pristine 0 gCO2/kWh, establishing a profound contrast against the GB-wide carbon intensity of 130 gCO2/kWh. Nevertheless, interconnector limits mean local abundance cannot freely flow to southern demand centers. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 32191.4 MWh, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £794,927 paid to switch off wind assets. Because that suppressed volume must be replaced by dispatchable generation elsewhere, an estimated 6116366.0 m3 of gas was burned elsewhere to replace it, adding an avoidable 11267.0 tonnes CO2 to the atmosphere. This stark dynamic exposes the dual penalty of current transmission constraints: energy consumers bear substantial financial balancing expenses, while avoidable fossil fuel combustion actively undermines the environmental advantages of Scotland’s zero-carbon generation.
